query: Which per-subject HRF estimation method and basis set should be pre-registered to capture HRF variability across diverse stimuli?

response.query: Which per-subject HRF estimation method and basis set should be pre-registered to capture HRF variability across diverse stimuli?
response.answer: To capture HRF variability across diverse stimuli, use the generalized linear model (GLM) with flexible basis functions pre-registered. This method accommodates individual differences in HRF shapes.

results.title: Correcting Task fMRI Signals for Variability in Baseline ...
results.content: Here the *Z(AUC)*j**residual,i** is the remaining task fMRI signal (i.e., “sensitized BOLD” in Figure 1) for *j*th voxel in segment *i* that more accurately estimates the task-induced BOLD activity after accounting for the voxel specific (i.e., brain area) age-related variability in baseline CBF signal (*CBF**measured*). As such, in our study we are attempting to correct for age-related variability in baseline CBF, and when we approach this problem using the individual subject voxel-wise normalization by division (i.e. CBF), we found that – (i) visual inspection of the resulting maps are more or less similar to ‘standard’ BOLD maps wherein false positives were retained, true positives were not identified, and in fact, the normalization by division approach removed some key task-specific areas (see figures in Supplementary Section S4), and (ii) The predictability of behavior using voxel-wise normalization by division approach was significantly weaker compared to the proposed methodology.
